To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic ethanol ingestion increased GABA(A) receptor function in acutely isolated amygdala neurons, but had no effect on strychnine sensitive glycine receptor function.

chronic ethanol exposure increases the functional expression of the GABA(A) receptor in acutely isolated adult lateral/basolatar amygdala neurons, without affecting strychnine sensitive glycine receptors.

chronic ethanol exposure increases the functional expression of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA)A receptors in acutely dissociated lateral/basolaterl amygdala neurons but does not affect the functional expression of strychnine sensitive glycine receptors.

the effects of chronic alcohol consumption on the expression of GABA and glycine receptors in the amygdala.

the neuroadaptations of GABA(A)/strychnine-sensitive glycines receptors in the lateral and basolateral amydgala following chronic ethanol exposure.

the effects of chronic alcohol on GABA(A), strychnine sensitive glycine receptors are complex and depend on the subunit composition.
